name: Logic
description: Logic is a highly strategic deduction-based card game for four players in two teams. It is a game of perfect information (eventually), where players must deduce the identity and position of cards in their opponents' hands. Unlike traditional trick-taking games, 'Logic' is more akin to a competitive version of Mastermind or Hanabi, requiring careful observation of partners' clues and opponents' guesses.
deck: 24 cards (A-Q from two suits, e.g., Hearts and Spades)

history.origins: Developed in the late 20th century as a competitive abstract deduction exercise. It gained popularity in programming and mathematics circles as a test of logical inference.
timeline: 1980s: Variations of 'Logic' (sometimes called 'Deduction') appear in university gaming clubs.
2004: Standardized rules for the 24-card version are published on game archive sites.
Present: Played online and in strategy forums as a pure mental challenge.
history.cultural: Regarded as a 'Brain' game, often used as a training exercise for pattern recognition.
history.evolution: The game was simplified from a 52-card version to ensure that rounds are fast and the state-space is manageable for high-level human memory.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (A+C vs B+D).
setup.deck: 24 cards: Ace (low) through Queen (high) of two suits (e.g., Red and Black).
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 6 cards face-down. They arrange their cards in front of them in **ascending order of value** from left to right.
setup.equipment: Standard deck and privacy screens for card arrangement.

rules.objective: Be the first player to correctly declare the identities of all cards still in play.
rules.gameplay: 1. **The Show**: Your partner privately shows you one of their face-down cards. You now know its identity and position. 2. **The Guess**: You must guess the identity of one of your OPPONENTS' face-down cards (Position + Rank). 3. **The Reveal**: If correct: The opponent turns the card face-up permanently. If incorrect: YOU must choose one of your own face-down cards to reveal face-up. 4. **Winning Declaration**: A player can 'Declare' at any time. They must correctly identify EVERY remaining face-down card in the game (teammates and opponents). If they get even one wrong, their team loses immediately.
keyRules: Cards arranged in ascending order left to right.
Partner shows you one card (identity and position).
Guess opponent's card by position and rank.
Correct guess: opponent reveals that card.
Incorrect guess: you must reveal one of your own cards.
Can declare at any time to name all remaining face-down cards.
Declaration must be 100% correct or your team loses.

strategy.basic: Use the ascending order to your advantage. If an opponent reveals a 10 at Position 4 (out of 6), you know that Positions 1-3 MUST be lower than 10, and Positions 5-6 MUST be higher than 10.
strategy.intermediate: The Partner Signal: When your partner shows you a card, they are often showing you a 'boundary' card (like a 6 or 7). Use this to deduce their other cards and narrow down the possibilities for the opponents.
strategy.advanced: Elimination Logic: If you know your team has both Aces, and no opponent has revealed an Ace yet, you can 'waste' a guess on an opponent's first position to see if they reveal a 2 or 3. Even an incorrect guess on your part provides information to your partner.
tips: Always track which ranks have been fully revealed (both suits). Once both Queens are face-up, they are out of the deck possibilities.
Be careful with your 'Self-Reveal' when you guess wrong. Reveal cards that you think your partner already deduced to give the opponents the least amount of new info.
